learning.learning_goal: Understand at least as an inclusive minimum and represent it with words, a number line, and a greater-than-or-equal-to inequality.
learning.big_idea: At least names the lowest allowed value. The boundary counts, and every greater value counts too.
novice_success_criteria: identify the minimum boundary from context
connect the closed point, rightward direction, and greater-than-or-equal-to symbol

screens.label: Lesson 010 · Prototype
screens.title: What does “at least” allow?
screens.body: Imagine a job requiring at least 30 training hours. Thirty hours qualifies, and any amount above 30 qualifies. Amounts below 30 do not.
screens.callout: No number-line or inequality notation is assumed. A number line puts smaller numbers to the left and larger numbers to the right. We will mark the allowed values before choosing a symbol.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Do not let the word “least” point you toward smaller values.
screens.prompt: A ride requires a height of at least 48 inches. Which height qualifies?

choices.feedback: At least includes the minimum itself, so exactly 48 inches qualifies along with every greater height.

hints: Ask whether the exact requirement is allowed.
At least means the minimum or more, not less than the minimum.

screens.label: Observe
screens.title: Build the allowed set from the minimum.

visual.ariaLabel: A number line with a closed point at 30 and an arrow extending right toward greater values
visual.caption: 30 is included; values greater than 30 are included
visual.message: The closed point includes the minimum. The arrow shows every greater value also works.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: Which description matches the number line?

visual.ariaLabel: A number line with a closed point at 18 and an arrow extending right
visual.message: Start at 18, include it, and continue toward greater values.

choices.feedback: The closed point includes 18, and the rightward arrow includes every value greater than 18.

hints: Read the point first, then follow the arrow.
Rightward values are greater on this number line.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Name the minimum, boundary, and allowed values.

visual.ariaLabel: A number line with a closed point at 21 extending toward greater values
visual.message: The boundary is 21. It is included, and greater values are allowed.

screens.phraseMeaning: The boundary value is allowed, and so is every greater value

definitions.meaning: the lowest value that is allowed in the situation
a limit whose exact value is part of the allowed set
the boundary value or any value larger than it

screens.guidance: Before choosing a symbol, test the exact boundary and one value on each side of it.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Minimum, included, then more.
screens.hook: At least = the minimum counts, and more counts.
screens.body: Rebuild the inequality from what the situation allows instead of reacting to the word least.
rebuildSteps: Test the exact boundary; at least includes it.
Mark a closed point because the boundary counts.
Extend toward greater values, then choose ≥.
screens.boundary: This reconstruction applies to an inclusive minimum. More than uses the same greater direction but excludes the boundary and uses an open point with >.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Choose the statement for “at least 12.”

visual.ariaLabel: A number line including 12 and extending to greater values
visual.message: Twelve is allowed, and values to its right are allowed.

choices.feedback: The greater side matches values above 12, and the line under the symbol includes 12 itself.

hints: The symbol needs both the greater direction and equality.

screens.label: Reveal
screens.title: The symbol compresses the allowed set.

visual.ariaLabel: A closed point at 12 with an arrow toward greater values
visual.message: Closed point = equal is allowed. Right arrow = greater values are allowed.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: Test values before choosing the inequality.
screens.prompt: A program requires at least 6 completed classes. Which statement is correct?

choices.feedback: Six is the included minimum, seven is greater and qualifies, while five falls below the requirement.

hints: Then test one value below and one above 6.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Reason without the model.
screens.prompt: A bank account must keep at least $100. Which balance breaks the rule?

choices.feedback: Ninety-nine dollars is below the included $100 minimum, so it is the only balance that breaks the rule.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Reconstruct the symbol from meaning.
screens.prompt: Why does “at least 25” use ≥ rather than >?

choices.text: Because the word least always means greater
Because 25 itself is allowed, so equality must be included
choices.feedback: The line under ≥ records that the exact boundary value belongs to the solution set.

choices.text: Because every value below 25 is allowed

hints: The difference between ≥ and > is whether equality counts.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Apply the boundary in a new setting.
screens.prompt: A delivery earns free shipping with an order of at least $50. Which orders receive free shipping?

choices.feedback: The $50 boundary is included and $72 is above it; $49 is below the minimum.

hints: Test $50 before comparing the other amounts.
Include the boundary and every greater order total.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: Which explanation shows understanding?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains at least.

choices.text: It names an included minimum and allows every greater value.
It always points toward smaller values because it contains least.
It excludes the named value and allows only larger ones.

hints: Name the kind of boundary first.
Check whether the exact value is included.

screens.title: You built “at least” from an inclusive minimum.
screens.body: You connected context, boundary testing, a closed point, greater values, and the ≥ symbol.
screens.nextRecommendation: Continue to no more than and contrast an included maximum with this included minimum.
